grades.lesson: For modular kit pieces, lock the world scale and camera framing to the kit grid rather than auto-fitting the model to the frame. Then verify that the footprint renders at identical pixel size at both the minimum and maximum of every size-changing knob.

flaws: Every tier uses the same window treatment. Upper tiers are just scaled-down copies, so the silhouette reads as stacked repeats rather than a tapering pagoda with a distinct ground hall.
At 5 tiers the top tier is cramped: its windows nearly collide with the pillars and the shortened finial loses presence.
In the dark brand probe, lime pillars against a violet roof plus a cyan finial make a garish triad. The pillar and finial colours follow brand slots with no harmony check.
The lanterns and plinth steps are tiny at the kit camera distance and read as noise rather than detail.
No render shows the lights-off state or the 3-tier minimum, so the lights knob and the low end of the tier range are unverified.
grades.lesson: When brand colours drive secondary roles such as trim, pillars and finials, derive them from the primary hue (shade, tint or analogous shift) or clamp their saturation. Mapping raw brand slots straight onto parts produces clashing triads in some brand probes.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. An octagonal park gazebo with posts, a railing and a pointed roof (cone). Footprint 4x4. Knobs: post colour, roof colour, size.

warnings: knobs with very subtle effect: lights

flaws: The entry step is a grid-aligned rectangular slab stuck onto the front-right corner of an octagonal plinth. It does not follow the octagon face it serves, it overhangs the base, and it reads as a pasted-on box rather than a stair.

The roof face shading ramps too far. The right-hand faces blow out to near-white (pale pink at defaults, almost white-blue in Seaside), so the roof silhouette loses contrast against the light background and the cone stops reading as one material.
In the dark brand probe the eave underside turns black and shows as dark wedges poking out at the left and right roof corners. It looks like a rendering artifact, not a design choice.
The dark brand probe also applies brand colours too literally: black posts and rails, lime roof and cyan finial. The result is garish and no longer matches the town-shop palette the brief asks for.
The lanterns are bare yellow cubes stuck to the sides of posts at inconsistent heights. They read as floating debris rather than fixtures.

The size knob at maximum barely changes the footprint. It mostly flattens the roof pitch and shifts proportions, so the knob gives little useful range, and at max the step starts colliding with the plinth edge.
The white plinth under the brown deck adds a second stacked base with no clear purpose, making the base look doubled.
The preset name 'Tram' is meaningless for a gazebo and looks carried over from another asset.
grades.lesson: Any attachment such as a stair, door, sign or lantern must be positioned and oriented relative to the specific face of the host geometry it serves (its normal and edge midpoint), not snapped to the world grid. Check it at every size extreme so it never overhangs or interpenetrates the base.

flaws: Preset 'Park' renders pixel-identical to defaults, so it is a dead preset that adds nothing.

The 'every knob at max' render barely differs from defaults: the gazebo is nearly the same size, with only slightly altered post and roof proportions. The size knob has almost no visible range, so a designer cannot tell it works.
The dark brand probe comes out as a washed-out lime roof with pale grey posts. No dark value survives, so the asset does not carry a dark brand identity.
In the dark probe, the finial turns cyan on top of a lime roof, producing a clashing, unintentional-looking colour pairing.
The model sits small in frame, filling roughly a third of the canvas with large empty margins, which weakens it as a standalone preview.
The roof is a faceted octagonal pyramid rather than the cone the brief asks for, and its low pitch with a heavy overhang makes the silhouette squat.
The interior floor is a flat tan or grey slab that reads muddy through the railings, and the lanterns look tacked onto the posts rather than designed in.
grades.lesson: Before submitting, diff every preset and every knob extreme against the defaults. If a preset is identical or a knob's max is barely distinguishable, either widen its range or remove it, because a control that visibly does nothing reads as broken to buyers.

flaws: The size knob barely does anything. The all-max render is almost the same size as defaults. Only the cone gets taller, and the base reads slightly narrower, so the briefed 'size' control fails at its extreme.

Lighting washes the front-facing roof-skirt facets to near white in every render. The roof colour reads only on the cone and the back of the skirt, which weakens the one knob that defines each preset. In the dark-brand probe the lime skirt fades to almost pure white.
The object sits small and low in the frame, with a large empty band above. At defaults it does not read as a centred hero asset.
The interior floor is mostly flat white plinth. Deck boards show only as a patch toward the entrance, so the floor looks unfinished rather than decked.
The lanterns are bolted to the outside of two adjacent posts on one side only. Their placement looks arbitrary rather than designed, and they cannot be controlled or switched off.
The presets are pure roof recolours: deck tone changes slightly, posts never change. They add little range beyond the roof-colour knob itself.
The base plinth and steps stay fixed white in every render. Even in the dark-brand probe there is no way to tie them to the palette.
grades.lesson: Render every knob alone at its minimum and maximum, and confirm each produces a clearly visible change in the object. A knob whose extreme looks the same as the default is a broken knob.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A delivery van with a tall cargo box, a logo panel and rear doors. Footprint 5x2. Knobs: body colour, logo colour, length 4-6 m, lights.

flaws: Emblem choice 'leaf' is broken. It renders as an unreadable dripping blue shape that reads as a glitch, not a leaf.
The 'Courier' preset is pixel-identical to the defaults, so it adds no value.
At maximum length the logo panel does not reposition or scale with the cargo box. It sits toward the cab and leaves a large blank cream expanse behind it, so the composition looks unfinished.
A grey recess or gap shows between the cab and the cargo box side, worse at maximum length. It reads as a missing face rather than intentional detailing.
The front wheel sits proud of the cab's front corner instead of under it, which makes the cab look mis-seated on the chassis.
The rear doors named in the brief are not legible from the shipped camera angle.
In the dark brand probe, body, cab, grille and chassis all collapse into similar greys. The grille and front detailing lose definition, and only the lime accent carries the image.
grades.lesson: Render every option of every choice knob at the shipped camera and size before submitting, and confirm that each one reads as the thing it is named for. Also make dependent elements, like logos and panels, reflow or re-centre when a size knob changes, so they do not stay anchored to their default position.

flaws: The 'emblem' choice knob does nothing. Setting it to 'house' renders pixel-identical to the defaults, with the same three generic dashes, so the knob is broken.
The logo panel at defaults is just three blue dashes in a frame. It reads as a placeholder, not a logo or emblem a designer would want to show.

At maximum range values the rear end breaks. A loose stripe fragment floats at the top of the rear doors. The doors and tail lights shift out of alignment with the box edge. The lower bumper and step look misregistered against the stretched body.

The cab does not read as a van cab. Behind the cargo box it shows as a flat grey deck with a small floating white roof piece and a tiny window. The silhouette looks more like a box on a flatbed than a delivery van.
The rear wheel block overlaps the bottom corner of the logo panel and the body skirt, so the wheel and body geometry visibly collide.

In the dark brand probe the lime logo colour sits on a white panel with weak contrast, and the brand colour is not used to give the body a dark treatment. The probe looks washed out rather than branded.
The 'lights' knob shows no visible lit or unlit difference across the renders. The orange roof markers look the same in every render.
The presets differ only in hue (blue, green, red). None of them shows off length, emblem or lights, so the presets show very little range.
grades.lesson: Before shipping, render every option of every choice knob and diff it against the defaults. Any option that produces an identical image is a broken knob, so fix it or remove it.

flaws: The 'emblem' choice knob does nothing. The 'house' render is pixel-identical to the defaults, and the logo stays three generic dashes in every render. It is a dead control, and the logo panel reads as a placeholder rather than a logo.

At max range values the rear doors come loose from the cargo box. The door panels protrude past the box corner and bumper, a stray blue stripe fragment floats above the door tops, and the amber roof markers shift off the box edge. The parts do not follow the length parameter.
The cab is badly underdeveloped. It reads as an open grey flatbed with a thin white slab and a small window block, so the silhouette says pickup or flatbed more than delivery van.
The wheels are flat dark cubes with white squares and read as crates, not wheels.
The 'lights' knob from the brief shows no distinguishable effect in any render. The red and amber markers look the same throughout.
The presets only recolour the trim stripe and slightly tint the body. All of them are the same van in a different accent, with no real variety.
grades.lesson: Attach every sub-part (doors, trim, lights) to the parametric dimensions it sits on, not to fixed coordinates, and confirm each knob changes the render by diffing min, max and every choice value against the defaults before submitting.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A clock tower: square brick tower with a clock face on the front, a belfry and pointed roof. Footprint 4x4. Knobs: brick colour, roof colour, height 8-16 m, lights.

flaws: Broken stacking geometry. Above the ground stage the left face of the tower is missing. A large white top slab is exposed where the clock stage wall should continue up, so the tower reads as a hollow L-shape rather than a solid square shaft. This shows in every render.

The clock face, the hero element, is illegible. The hour markers are irregular black blobs scattered around a gear-toothed disc rather than evenly spaced ticks. At thumbnail size it reads as a cookie or a cog, not a clock.

The front clock crowds into the corner quoins instead of sitting centred on its face with a margin. In 'four sides', the left clock floats over the exposed-slab region and makes the missing-wall problem more obvious.
Quoin blocks are drawn as detached cubes that hover off the wall edges, especially down the left silhouette. They do not read as stones bonded into the corner.
The door lamps are tiny floating squares with no visible bracket.
Preset 'Classic' is pixel-identical to the defaults, so it is a wasted preset.

At maximum height the clock shrinks relative to the tower and sits awkwardly close to the belfry. The extra height is just repeated windows with no stage articulation such as a string course or a change of set-back.
Dark brand probe: the dark walls swallow the quoin and wall contrast on the shaded left face, and the teal clock rim clashes with the purple roof. It is usable but not tuned.
grades.lesson: When a building is assembled from stacked stages, model each stage as a closed box and check every visible face in the actual camera view at defaults and extremes. An exposed internal top surface where a wall should be is the most obvious defect a buyer will see.

flaws: At maximum height the tower breaks. A white floor slab is exposed partway up the shaft, the upper storey's walls are missing or inset, and two windows sit on that bare slab. It reads as a sliced model, not a taller tower.
At maximum height the pilasters and string courses do not run continuously across the added section. The extra height looks bolted on rather than generated as part of the tower.
The maximum-height render is framed so the 4x4 footprint shrinks noticeably. Set beside town-shop pieces, it is hard to confirm that the tower actually stays on the 6 m grid.
The open belfry interior renders as flat dark panels with odd slit artefacts on the left opening. It reads as a hole in the mesh rather than a lit or shadowed space.
The flat white deck around the roof base is the brightest surface on the model in every render. It pulls the eye away from the clock.
The Harbour preset's saturated primary-blue roof and finials clash with its muted grey-blue walls and look toy-like next to the other presets.
There is no visible difference to tell whether the 'lights' knob does anything. The lit window and lanterns look the same in every render.
There is no knob for clock time or clock face colour, so the hands are frozen in every variant.
The brick colour knob has no texture or coursing at any value, so the 'brick' tower is indistinguishable from render or stucco.
grades.lesson: When a knob adds height by stacking modules, render the maximum and several intermediate values. Check that every module's walls, trim and pilasters fully close over internal floor slabs, so no interior faces are ever exposed.

flaws: The clock faces, the hero feature, have serrated, sawtooth rims in every render. They read as gears or aliasing artefacts, not clean dials.
The white floor slabs cut through the shaft and stick out past the brick like shelves. The walls between them look missing, so the tower reads as a dollhouse cutaway, not a solid brick tower.
Upper-floor windows sit at odd angles and float on the white bands. The facade looks unassembled.
At max height the clock faces press against the slab below and look cramped. The extra height becomes repeated identical white bands, not a more convincing tower.
In the dark brand probe the clock face fill turns dark brown with dark hands, which is nearly illegible. The belfry interior goes pure black and reads as a hole.
The light brand probe recolours the trim to grey-green and the brick to pale beige. The brick texture almost disappears and the tower loses its 'brick' identity.
The brief asks for a clock face on the front, but a second face is placed on the side with no knob to control it.
Knobs are limited to colours, height and lights. There is no control for clock count or face, belfry openness, or roof pitch, which a kit piece would benefit from.
grades.lesson: Build the focal detail of an asset (a dial, logo plate or emblem) from true smooth geometry at enough resolution. Inspect its silhouette at final render size in every palette, because a jagged or low-contrast hero element sinks the whole piece regardless of overall form.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A windmill with a tapered tower, cap and four sails made of thin boxes. Footprint 4x4. Knobs: tower colour, sail colour, height, sail angle.

flaws: At max knobs the sails break down. The lattice turns into dense, jagged white fragments that read as rendering noise, not slats. The enlarged sail span also crowds the shrunken cap and the hub collides with the roof.
Preset 'Polder' renders pixel-identical to defaults, so it is a wasted preset that offers the buyer nothing.
Brand theming is inconsistent. In the light probe the sail frames switch to cream. In the dark probe they stay default brown against lime panels, so frame colour is neither fixed nor reliably themed.
The door is a vertical box glued to a tapered tower. At the base it pokes out past the tower silhouette instead of sitting in the wall.
At defaults the left sail sweeps directly across the upper window, half-hiding it. Window placement ignores the sail plane.
The sail angle knob shows no visible change at max. Either the range is 0–90° and lands back on the same symmetric pose, or it isn't wired. Either way the extreme shows nothing.
A stray thin vertical line appears beside the door/tower edge (around mid-height, right side) in default, Polder, gable and dark-probe renders.
The window glow and plinth do not respond to the brand probes. The dark tower with fixed warm-yellow windows and a light-grey plinth looks unconsidered rather than intentional.
grades.lesson: Before shipping, render every count/density and angle knob at its max and check that repeated detail stays above a legible minimum size at the asset's real display scale. Make sure the extreme pose actually differs from the default, for example by keeping a rotation range under the shape's symmetry period.

flaws: At max knobs the sails break apart into jagged, stair-stepped fragments. The lattice slats read as scattered pixel crumbs rather than four clean rotated sails. They look broken, not stylised.
At max height the sails do not scale with the tower. They become noticeably undersized and lose the windmill silhouette.
The 'gable' cap reads as a house roof dropped onto a round tower. It overhangs well past the tower on one side, has no finial and does not match the octagonal geometry, so it looks unintentional.
The windows at max height are duplicated in rigid twin columns, which makes the taller tower look like a lighthouse or apartment block rather than a windmill.
The dark brand probe puts lime-green sail cloth against brown frames and a near-black tower. Legible, but harsh. Sail cloth would sit better as a tinted neutral than a raw accent.
At defaults the asset fills only a small part of the frame, with no visible ground or footprint plate. The 4x4 footprint the brief asks for cannot be checked by eye.
grades.lesson: When a knob rotates a composite part (sails, blades, arms), group its sub-boxes and rotate the group as one unit around a single pivot. Then render that knob at non-90° angles and at its extreme to confirm thin members stay straight and attached. Do not rotate or snap each sub-box on its own.

flaws: At max height the whole model is auto-fitted down. The 4x4 grass tile shrinks from about 165px to about 125px wide, and the annex and door shrink with it. This breaks the brief's requirement to match town-shop scale on the 6 m grid, so the piece will not tile alongside other kit pieces.

At maximum, the sail angle knob renders the sails in the same cross orientation as the default. A four-sail rotor is 90° symmetric, so the range's extreme reads as unchanged. The useful range is only about 0–45°.

The sail colour knob only recolours the slat infill. The heavy brown frames stay fixed in every preset and probe. In the dark probe this gives lime slats inside brown wood under a purple cap, which is garish and reads as unrelated colours rather than a palette.

The dark brand probe turns the tower near-black against a mid-grey canvas with a purple roof. It is legible, but it reads as a novelty recolour rather than a considered dark variant. The pale grass tile is untouched, so the base clashes with the dark tower.
The dome cap is a stack of stepped octagonal plates. It reads as a crude ziggurat or beehive rather than a dome, and it is noticeably rougher than the conical cap.
At defaults, the lower sail's tip comes down onto the annex roof ridge. The sweep looks like it would collide with the annex as the sails rotate, which suggests nobody checked clearance.
The tower's taper is a set of visibly offset rings with bright seam lines that bulge unevenly on the left. The secondary props beside the annex (white sacks or crates) are too small to read.
The model sits low and small in the frame, occupying roughly a third of the canvas. At defaults there is a lot of dead space above and to the sides.
grades.lesson: For pieces in a shared grid kit, lock a fixed world-to-pixel scale and anchor point across all knob values; never auto-fit the model to the frame. Fitting rescales the footprint and breaks tiling with sibling pieces. Size knobs should grow the object within the canvas instead.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A striped lighthouse on a rocky base with a glowing lamp room. Footprint 4x4. Knobs: stripe colours, height 8-14 m, stripes 2-5, lights.

flaws: Dark brand probe: the lamp-room roof, gallery and railing flip to near-white. Against the pale grey background they lose their silhouette, so the top third of the tower dissolves and the amber glass has little contrast against white trim.
Preset 'Harbour' renders pixel-identical to Defaults. It is a wasted preset that shows no extra range.
At defaults the single window straddles a red/cream stripe boundary and the door top butts against a boundary. Openings look dropped onto the shaft rather than placed relative to the stripes.

The rocky base is sparse and lopsided. There are a few chunky rocks front-left and right, little behind, and a thin white plinth sliver shows under the door. It does not read as a convincing 4x4 footprint base.
The gallery railing posts are sparse and unevenly spaced, so the balcony reads unfinished at this scale.
The object sits low and small in frame with a large empty top margin, which is weak thumbnail composition for a marketplace asset.
Minimum height, minimum stripe count and the lights-off state are not demonstrated. The 'lights' knob cannot be verified and the low extremes are untested.
Usefulness is narrow: a single landmark piece for one town kit, with only colour/height/stripe variation.
grades.lesson: When trim or secondary colours are derived automatically from brand inputs (e.g. auto-contrast inks), check their contrast against the scene background as well as against neighbouring fills. Otherwise silhouette-defining parts like roofs and outlines can vanish in light or dark brand probes.

flaws: Breaks kit scale at max height. The whole model is shrunk to fit the frame: the rock base narrows from about 155px to 140px wide and the lamp room gets smaller. On a fixed 6 m grid this piece will no longer match town-shop or its 4x4 footprint.
At max settings, all three upper tower windows disappear, leaving only the ground-floor window. Window placement seems tied to stripe bands and gets silently dropped instead of redistributed.
The windows read as hexagonal blocks stuck onto the tower surface rather than openings set into the masonry.
The topmost window collides with the underside of the gallery at defaults.
The mix of lit (orange) and unlit (grey-blue) windows looks arbitrary rather than designed.
Dark brand probe: the tower body, base and lamp-room gallery all go near-black. The gallery railing, platform and tower merge into one mass, and the silhouette loses its structure.
Stripe bands do not terminate cleanly under the gallery. The top band is partly hidden, so the stripe rhythm looks cropped rather than planned.
The lamp-room 'glow' is only flat orange panels, with no light falloff or emissive cue. It reads the same as the windows, so the brief's 'glowing lamp room' is under-delivered.
grades.lesson: For modular kit pieces on a fixed world grid, keep the world-unit-to-pixel scale constant across every knob value. Never auto-fit the model to the frame. Also, re-lay-out dependent details like windows from the new dimensions instead of dropping them when a knob changes.

flaws: Lamp room: the glowing cream cubes stick out past the lantern and gallery rail (upper right and left), so they read as stray, detached geometry rather than a light or beam. This shows in every render.
The brown door is a freestanding slab with its own dark canopy, set forward of the tower wall. It looks pasted next to the building instead of set into it.
A small white sliver pokes out at the bottom-right corner of the rocky base in the defaults, all presets and both brand probes. It looks like a z-fighting or overhang artifact.
The tower sits on a cream plinth that has its own window, and the bottom stripe band hangs over it as a skirt. The joint between plinth and shaft is muddled and reads as two unrelated parts.

Dark brand probe: the light stripe goes mid-grey against dark green, and the roof and gallery go grey too. The lighthouse turns muddy and loses its signature high-contrast stripes. The light stripe colour needs a floor on lightness, independent of the brand.

At the max setting the base switches from the blocky rock mass to a flat scattered-rock ring. That changes the silhouette so much it no longer reads as the same kit piece. The base footprint also looks smaller than the 4x4 cells the brief asks for, which risks misalignment with town-shop scale.
The 'lights' knob makes no visible difference across the renders shown. It is unclear what it controls, and the lantern glow is never readable as an actual light.
grades.lesson: Every sub-part (glows, doors, trims, plinths) must be anchored to a parent surface and contained within its housing at every parameter value. Before submitting, scan each render's silhouette for floating, protruding or detached fragments and for single-pixel slivers at footprint corners.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A pond tile 6x6: grass edge, water as a thin pale blue box, lily pads, reeds, a little wooden jetty. Knobs: water colour, lily pads 0-8, jetty toggle.

warnings: knobs with very subtle effect: pads, lights

flaws: The jetty is structurally incoherent in every render. Planks and rails float at odd angles, the deck pieces don't connect to each other, and one section sits off the pond rim over grass. It reads as broken geometry, not a jetty.
The water is visibly split into separate boxes with seam lines across the surface. It does not read as one continuous pond.
The pond is small and off-centre on the 6x6 tile, leaving large empty grass areas. The white rim reads as concrete or snow rather than the grass edge the brief asks for.
The lily pad knob shows no visible effect. Only about 2 pads appear at defaults and still about 2-3 at max, against a stated range of 0-8.
At max, a stray brown reed/post sits alone on the grass at the back right, away from the pond.
At max, the extra reeds cluster in front of the lamp post and overlap it.
The Spring preset is pixel-identical to the defaults, so it adds nothing.
Light brand probe: the grass turns white and merges with the white rim, so the tile reads as a blank slab with no grass.
Dark brand probe: the water becomes acid lime-green and reads as lawn or toxic sludge, not water.
Dark brand probe: the jetty turns purple and the ground near-black, so the scene loses its pond identity.
The brief asked for grass edge, water, lily pads, reeds and jetty. The bench and lamp were added unasked and crowd the small pond.
grades.lesson: Build multi-part props like jetties, fences and stairs from a single local origin, with each piece positioned relative to its neighbour. Then check every render, including extremes, for floating, disconnected or out-of-bounds parts before submitting.

flaws: At maximum knobs, scattered props collide. Lily pads overlap each other, reeds spear straight through the lily-pad cluster near the front, and of the 8 pads requested only about 5 are distinguishable.
Reeds placed on the back grass edge sit right at the tile corner and are partly hidden behind it. They read as stray sticks poking over the rim, not intentional planting.
Cattail heads look detached from their stems on several reeds. The gap between the brown head and the green stalk makes them look like they are floating.

The brand probes recolour the wooden jetty to salmon or terracotta, so it no longer reads as wood. In the light probe the water becomes a saturated cyan that clashes with the muted town-kit palette the brief asks to match.
In the dark brand probe the lily pads are nearly the same dark green as the grass and lose contrast against the pale water. The probe also never actually produces a dark scene.
The Summer preset is almost indistinguishable from the defaults, so it is a wasted preset.
The water is a flat slab flush with the grass, with no edge, bank or depth cue. The pond reads as a painted rectangle rather than water set into a tile.
grades.lesson: Scattered props need placement rules that keep them in their intended zone, a minimum spacing so they never overlap each other or other objects, and a reserved clearance around fixed features like a jetty. Verify these rules hold at the maximum count, not just at the defaults.

flaws: The grass border is built from four strips that do not meet cleanly. Every render shows the same joint errors: notches at the left and right inner corners where the water shows through, and a protruding tan block at the front corner. There is also a visible step and seam where the front and left strips misalign. These are construction bugs, not style choices.
The water is so pale against the near-identical pale grey background that the pond barely reads as water at defaults. The tile loses contrast and presence.

The 'Moonlit' preset is nearly indistinguishable from the defaults. Only the greens darken slightly and the water shifts faintly toward lavender, with no sense of night. A preset that does not deliver its name is wasted.
In the light brand probe the brand colour lands on the grass, which turns khaki-beige and reads as sand or dead turf. The 'pond in a town' read is lost.
The lily-pad flowers are tiny single-colour cones that become illegible specks at tile scale, especially in the brand probes.
At the maximum render about six pads are distinguishable, not the 8 the brief allows. Pads are either occluded or overlapping, so the top of the knob range adds clutter rather than visible detail.
The jetty's connection to the grass edge sits right at a broken corner notch, so it looks like it attaches to nothing solid.
grades.lesson: When a perimeter or frame is assembled from separate boxes, explicitly resolve the corners. Either extend two strips to overlap the full corner, or add dedicated corner pieces. Then zoom in on every joint in at least one render before submitting. Misaligned joints read as broken geometry instantly, even when everything else is polished.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A small arched footbridge 6x3 over water: deck boxes stepping up and down, railings. Knobs: wood colour, rail colour, water toggle.

flaws: The deck does not read as an arch. It is a set of loosely stacked flat slabs. At defaults there are visible gaps where water shows through between the deck and the far railing near midspan.

At maximum range the stepped slabs separate into a floating staircase. The bottom-left slab pokes out past the railing line and the lantern post. The added support posts land at arbitrary points under the slabs, so the structure looks broken rather than more arched.
Railing top rails run nearly straight while the deck steps underneath. Rail and deck do not follow a shared profile, which undermines the 'arched footbridge' read.
Preset 'Kyoto' renders pixel-identical to the defaults. It is a dead preset.

In the dark brand probe the deck goes flat near-black with almost no top/side shading difference, collapsing into a silhouette. The neon lime is also applied to the railings and lantern caps, which looks garish and loses the wooden-bridge character.
In the light brand probe the deck turns near-white and the banks go flat grey, so the bridge loses its material read. Brand colour is being mapped onto wood and ground slots where it does not belong.
The water toggle requested in the brief is not demonstrated anywhere. Wood colour also does not appear to be independently controllable from the brand mapping.
Saturated flat blue water and white snow-like banks look unrelated to a town-kit palette. A small plant on the far left bank is half-hidden behind the bank edge.
grades.lesson: For any segmented or stepped geometry driven by a parameter, compute every segment from one continuous profile curve. Make adjacent pieces overlap or share edges, and attach railings and supports to that same curve. Then render the parameter's extremes and confirm nothing detaches, floats or pokes through.

flaws: The deck has a hole near the crest. Water shows through a square gap between the far deck boxes in the defaults, both presets and both brand probes, and it is most obvious with railing set to 'low'. A walkable footbridge piece with a visible hole in it is broken.
A stray thin dark bar lies diagonally on the near-left grass, parallel to the bridge. It reads as a misplaced plank or leftover geometry rather than an intentional detail.
The railing arcs are built from staircased voxel steps that look beaded and jagged at kit scale. This is noisier than the clean massing the rest of the piece uses.

The railing arc rises far above the stepped deck at mid-span and drops to ground level at the ends. Rail and deck profiles don't relate, so the rails look like hoops placed over the deck rather than attached to it.
At max ranges the deck runs right to the base edge. The near-left grass almost disappears and the end lantern sits on the lip, so the piece feels cramped against its 6 m tile.
The water-toggle state isn't evident in any render, so the brief's third knob can't be verified. Water stays the same blue in both brand probes and only one side of the channel is readable.
grades.lesson: When you build curved or stepped forms from discrete boxes, derive each box's position and length from its neighbours, with a small overlap, rather than from independent samples. Then render from the shipping camera at the defaults and at the extremes to confirm no gaps let the background or water show through.

flaws: The 'arch' is a stack of hovering boxes that step up and down like a ziggurat. There is no curved underside, no abutments and no supports, so the deck looks like floating steps rather than an arched footbridge.
The top rails follow the same jagged staircase steps, which reinforces the blocky stair read instead of a smooth arc.
The white dashes on the water look like road lane markings, which confuses what the surface is.
At max settings the near-left lantern post crowds the front railing, and the first deck step appears to overhang the bank awkwardly.
The presets (Lacquer, Park) only recolour the rails, so they add almost no range beyond the colour knob itself.
The water toggle the brief asked for is not demonstrated in any render, so a required knob is unverified.
In the dark brand probe the wood deck turns flat slate grey and no longer reads as timber. Brand mapping overrides material identity.
The small grass slabs, tiny reed and bush feel sparse and generic, so the piece does not show clear kit value at its scale.
grades.lesson: When the brief names a signature form (e.g. 'arched'), make the silhouette itself express it with ramped or curved geometry and a visible underside. Check that the form still reads at thumbnail size before adding details like lanterns or decorations.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A playground with a slide, swings frame and a sandbox on a soft mat. Footprint 6x6. Knobs: mat colour, slide colour, swings 1-3, sandbox toggle.

flaws: The sandbox geometry is broken at every setting. Raised mat tiles poke through the sand and the front sandbox wall. In Candy and Light they show as white blocks, and as green blocks at defaults.
A stepped slab at the front of the mat hangs over the white border instead of sitting inside the 6x6 footprint. It is most obvious as a black overhang in the dark brand probe.
The slide's side support is one large flat beige triangle that cuts through the tower and the ladder rails. It reads as a placeholder wedge, not a modelled structure.
The slide's exit pad runs past the mat onto the border trim.
Preset Park renders pixel-identical to the defaults, so the preset adds nothing.
In the light brand probe the white mat sits on the white border and white ground, so the base loses all definition. There is no outline or tonal step to separate them.
At max knobs the taller tower crowds the ladder, which becomes partly hidden behind the frame, and the slide wedge grows even larger.
The required sandbox toggle is never shown in its off state, so it is unverified. The knob set is otherwise thin for a kit piece, and colour knobs carry most of it.
grades.lesson: Lay out every sub-object from one shared footprint grid. Before shipping, check that no prop intersects another prop or the base tiles beneath it, and that nothing extends past the declared footprint edge.

flaws: Depth-ordering or placement bug in every render: the swing frame and slide tower sit at or beyond the mat's back edges, and the mat paints over their lower halves. The rear swing posts, the tower base and almost the whole slide are hidden. The posts look like they plunge through the floor.

The slide, a headline feature in the brief, reads only as a small pink, yellow or teal triangle peeking out behind the mat. The slide-colour knob is close to meaningless because so little of the slide is visible.
Swing seats are hidden behind the mat. Defaults show no seats at all, and the all-max render, which should show 3 swings, shows only one orange seat. The swings 1-3 knob cannot be read.
The composition is badly unbalanced: all the play equipment is crammed into the back corners, and the 6x6 mat is mostly empty except for the sandbox, so the tile looks unfinished.
With 'roof: open', the tower deck floats with posts cut off at the mat line. This makes the occlusion bug even more obvious.
The sandbox toggle is not demonstrated in any render, and there is no evidence the swings count actually changes the geometry.
grades.lesson: In isometric/3D kit pieces, keep every component inside the base footprint and draw in strict back-to-front depth order (or use a real depth buffer). Then check every render to confirm each feature named in the brief is fully visible and is not clipped by the floor or base.

flaws: The slide's run-out pad ends directly on the raised mat curb in every render (defaults, all presets, both probes). It grows longer at max and still collides. It reads as clipping, and a slide that dumps kids into a kerb is a design error a reviewer will spot instantly.
The slide is a solid filled wedge with no rails or lip. It reads as a ramp or tent, not a slide, and is the weakest object in an otherwise clean kit.
The bench is jammed against the right-hand curb with no clearance and partly sits on the border. The layout feels packed into the corner rather than composed.
Uneven composition at defaults: swings, tower, slide and bench crowd the back half while the front-left quadrant of the mat is empty.
Sandbox contents (shovel, bucket) are tiny, low-contrast slivers that disappear at thumbnail size. The bucket recolours with the brand but the shovel barely registers.
The light brand probe's near-white tiles lose almost all grid contrast, so the mat reads as a flat beige slab.
Knob set drifts from the brief. An unrequested roof choice and a bench appear, and none of the renders shows the sandbox toggle off, so its effect is unverified. Swing count is only legible at max.
grades.lesson: Compute every sub-object's full extent at the maximum of its knobs (run-outs, arcs, seats, overhangs) and enforce a clearance margin from the footprint border and from neighbouring objects before placing it. A collision visible in every render is an automatic reject.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A picket fence run with posts and pointed pickets. Footprint 6x0.5. Knobs: colour, height, length 2-6 m.

warnings: knobs with very subtle effect: lights

flaws: The 'scalloped' style choice is nearly indistinguishable from the default pointed style. The picket tops never form a readable scallop arc between posts, so the option promises a silhouette it does not deliver.
The 'Classic' preset renders identically to the defaults. It is a wasted preset slot that shows no new configuration.
The gate's concrete threshold pad protrudes forward of the 0.5 m base strip. This breaks the stated 6x0.5 footprint, so the piece will not tile cleanly on the 6 m kit grid.
The brief asked for a fence run, but the asset forces a centred gate with lantern posts and offers no knob to turn it off. A plain straight run, the most-needed kit piece, cannot be made.
The lantern caps stay a fixed dark grey across every palette. In the dark brand probe they read as unbranded leftovers next to the lime and purple.

No render is supplied at minimum length (2 m). The max-knob render shows the same run length as the defaults. Whether a centred gate plus four posts survives at 2 m is unverified, which is a real risk.
grades.lesson: Every choice-knob option must change the silhouette visibly at thumbnail size; render each option side by side with the default and drop or exaggerate any option a buyer could not tell apart at a glance.

flaws: The bright white base slab reads as a separate plinth or snow rather than ground. It adds a hard edge that will fight whatever tile it is placed on in a town scene.
Every post carries a glowing lantern cap. Across a long run this gets busy and makes a simple picket fence feel over-ornamented, and there is no knob to switch the caps off.
In 'gate: end' the gate is forced into the accent colour, so it reads as a different object from the run. The gate is also narrow, so its posts sit very close together and the end looks cramped.
The renders show no minimum-extreme case (2 m length, low height), so the short end of the length range is unverified.
grades.lesson: Ground a kit piece with a base that matches the kit's ground plane, not a contrasting slab. A high-contrast plinth makes the asset look pasted-on and hurts tiling with neighbouring pieces.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A flower cart with wheels and buckets of colourful flowers. Footprint 2x1.5. Knobs: cart colour, flower colours seed, buckets 3-8.

flaws: At defaults the lantern post stands dead centre on the front of the cart. It cuts across the purple-flower bucket and the front fascia, hiding the asset's hero content.
The left front awning post runs straight through the rear-left bucket and its flower in every render with a roof, so that bucket reads as clipped.

At maximum buckets (8) the flowers crowd and intersect. The lantern collides with the red flower, a bucket is hidden behind the lantern, the rear red flower overlaps the back awning post, and blooms jumble together with no readable arrangement.
Dark brand probe breaks the piece. The buckets render near-black and look like tar pails rather than flower buckets. The cart turns neon chartreuse, which reads garish rather than branded.
The Blossom preset washes the awning out to white with hairline pink lines. The striped canopy loses its read and looks unfinished.
The Market preset is pixel-identical to the defaults, so it adds no range.
Only one wheel is clearly legible. The rear-left wheel is a dark blocky mass that reads as an undefined shape, and the right side rests on a lone wooden post, so the cart's support looks lopsided.
The flowers are small relative to the cart mass. From the standard isometric angle the 'colourful flowers' payload barely registers next to the large green body.
grades.lesson: Place variable-count props into explicit slots that are checked against fixed obstacles (posts, poles, fixtures) and against each other, then verify the maximum count for collisions. Never let a decorative fixture occupy the zone where the subject's hero content sits.

flaws: The lamp post is buried inside the awning. With roof='none' the lamp head stands well above the deck at roughly awning height. With the roof on, only its yellow underside pokes out below the canopy, so the two meshes intersect.
There is too little clearance under the awning. The back-row flower stacks (yellow, blue, purple) reach right up to the awning's front edge and read as touching or clipping it at defaults.

At maximum buckets the layout breaks. Buckets crowd and overlap each other in the front row, and the flower stacks visually merge. The orange bucket at the right sits on the deck edge, over the rail, and reads as hanging off.

At maximum the red flower stack sits directly against the red awning edge and becomes indistinguishable from the canopy. The Harbour preset has the same merge between the yellow front stack and the yellow awning. Flower colours are not kept distinct from the awning colour.

The flower colours seed does not visibly vary across presets. Defaults, Blossom and Harbour all show the identical yellow/blue/purple/pink/orange arrangement, so presets only recolour the cart and awning.
The dark brand probe renders a light lavender awning and a lime deck. The cart colour mapping does not carry a dark brand's value range onto the piece, and it reads like a second light theme.
Some small details are ambiguous: the floating brown bracket on the left post, and the brown-topped pink 'flower' at maximum, which reads as a box rather than a bloom.
grades.lesson: Whenever a part can sit under or beside another part, or its count is driven by a knob, derive its placement and height from the real available volume. Use clearance to the roof and a deck-area grid, evaluated at the maximum knob values. Clamp spacing or count so nothing can intersect, overlap or overhang, and verify by rendering every optional sub-part both on and off.

flaws: One flower bucket position is sunk into the deck or tucked behind the rear rail. Only a lone flower-head cube shows, floating with no bucket or stem. It appears as a blue cube at defaults, a blue dot in Blossom, a pink cube in Harbour, a purple bit in the light probe and an orange bit in the dark probe. It reads as a stray voxel in every render.
At max buckets (8), the lavender cluster by the lantern sits on the rail edge with no visible bucket, so the same placement bug gets worse at higher counts.
The side sign carries a red cross that reads as a first-aid or medical symbol, not a florist mark. This is a semantic miss on a flower cart.
Dark brand probe: the cart body goes lime green under a saturated purple awning. The pairing is garish, and the green bucket leaves vanish against the lime deck.
The buckets turn flat grey in the dark probe and lose the clean white-tin read of the defaults.
The brown divider rod across the deck runs right behind the front buckets and visually skewers them at this angle.

Knobs are thin for a kit piece. There is no separate awning colour control exposed in the brief, no lantern or sign toggle, and the seed changes flower hue but not flower type or height, so variety stays limited.
grades.lesson: When scattering sub-objects (props, plants, items) across a surface, generate placement slots from the visible top face and reject any slot whose base would sit below the surface or behind an occluder (rails, posts, trim). Then render at the minimum and maximum counts to confirm every instance reads as a complete, grounded object.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A canal tile 6x6 with stone banks, water and a moored small boat. Knobs: stone colour, water colour, boat colour, boat toggle.

flaws: The boat, the hero element, does not read as a boat. It is a hollow rectangular U-frame with square ends, no bow taper, no hull curvature and no deck. At a glance it looks like a floating trough or a barrier.

At defaults the front-right lamp post sits directly in front of the boat's stern. Its head and pole cut through the boat silhouette, so the main subject is occluded in every render. The prop layout ignores the fixed isometric sightline.

At the max-knob render the enlarged boat runs into the left bank wall. Its rear corner clips into the stone edge, and one of the two bollards disappears behind or inside the hull. A size knob is allowed to exceed the water channel.
At max, the mooring line, a thick beige bar, now runs at an odd angle into the enlarged hull. It reads as a stray plank rather than a rope.

In the light brand probe the water becomes saturated coral-orange. It reads as lava or a red carpet, not water. Water colour is mapped straight to brand accent with no water-like constraint or tinting.
The bench on the right bank is a crude brown slab plus a black box. It is noticeably lower fidelity than the lamps and bollards.
The right bank has unexplained grey stepped striping and small light tick marks on its front face. They look like texture artifacts rather than intentional steps or masonry.

The presets (Amsterdam, Venice) only recolour. Venice's teal water and black boat are nice, but nothing about bank or boat form changes. The 'range knob' that scales the boat is not one the brief asked for, and it breaks the tile.
grades.lesson: Any knob that scales or moves an object must be clamped to the free space of its containing region (e.g. the water channel between bank walls, minus clearance for props). Verify the extreme value against the real geometry before shipping, not just the default.

flaws: boatStyle 'launch' is broken. A pink slab from the hull sits detached on top of the far bank coping. The small launch hull is jammed against the near bank, with the gangway plank passing through it.

bank 'steps' is broken. The bench sinks into the step, with its back and legs cut off by the step geometry. The far-right bank segment is disjointed from the rest of the bank, and the right lamp floats awkwardly on it.

At defaults the boat is a crude box hull. The tan plank crosses it at an arbitrary angle and appears to intersect it rather than rest on it as a gangway. The hull's far end seems to tuck under the left bank lip.
The 'every range knob at max' render is identical to defaults. Either there are no meaningful range knobs or they do nothing visible, so the asset has almost no parametric range beyond recolouring.
The dark brand probe recolours the boat to a neon lime that glows against the grey stone. It is off-palette for a town kit and looks like a selection highlight, not a painted boat.
The water colour stays the same saturated cornflower blue in both brand probes. Stone and boat adapt but water does not, so the probes feel half-applied.
The far bank overhangs the water edge on the right, so the tile does not read as a clean 6x6 grid piece that will tile seamlessly with neighbours.
Lamps, bench and bollard are added beyond the brief. They have no toggle, which limits reuse when the tile is placed next to other street furniture.
grades.lesson: Render every option of every choice knob and inspect it for detached or interpenetrating parts. When a variant swaps a sub-assembly (a hull, a bank profile), derive the positions of everything attached to it (props, ropes, planks, furniture) from the new part's actual bounds rather than reusing the default variant's coordinates.

flaws: Water reads as a road. The straight white dashes on a flat blue slab look like lane markings, not ripples, so the canal is mistaken for a street at first glance.

The boat is malformed at defaults. It is a stubby boxy block with a disconnected thin red sliver trailing along the quay, plus a lamp-like post rising from it. It does not read as a small moored boat and appears to clip into the left bank wall.
Broken at max knobs. The thin hull plank detaches and juts diagonally across the canal, crossing open water, so the geometry is clearly broken.
The boat is the only element that changes across Amsterdam, Venice and the brand probes, and it looks equally crude in every version. Colour cannot rescue the form.
The bench on the right bank sits on the curb lip edge rather than set back on the walkway, which reads as misplaced.
The front tile edge shows a flat water plane with only a thin dark stroke. It has none of the visible depth or bank thickness the stone sides have, so it is inconsistent as a kit tile.
The brief's knob set (stone, water, boat colour, boat toggle) is honoured, but an unexplained range knob deforms the boat geometry and breaks it. It does not belong, or its range is unsafe.
grades.lesson: Build compound props (hull, cabin, mast) as children positioned relative to one parent anchor, and render every geometry-affecting knob at both extremes before submitting. Parts that drift apart or leave the tile bounds are an automatic reject.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A clipped hedge run with a gate gap option. Footprint 6x1. Knobs: leaf colour, height 0.6-1.8 m, gate toggle.

flaws: The hedge does not read as a hedge. Each run is a smooth extruded box with no foliage break-up, no clipped-edge softening and no leaf texture. At town scale it reads as a green shipping container or a windowed building.
The pink (Formal: white) squares sit flush on the flat faces in a sparse, regular pattern. They read as windows or vents, not flowers or berries, which reinforces the 'building' reading.

Gate posts do not scale with hedge height. At max height the left post is swallowed by the hedge block and only its cap pokes out. The right post sits well below the hedge top. The gate looks undersized and wedged in.
At defaults the left gate post already intersects and hides behind the left hedge block. The gate geometry is not cleanly seated in the gap.
The orange latch is a small floating square that does not connect convincingly to the gate leaf.
Preset 'Garden' renders identically to the defaults. It is a wasted preset.
The height knob's visible range is timid. Max barely differs from the default. The low 0.6 m end, which would be the most useful variant, is not demonstrated.
The topiary option drops faceted low-poly cones onto otherwise smooth boxes. It is a style mismatch, and the pieces look placed on top rather than grown from the hedge.

The dark brand probe maps the leaf colour to acid lime with a violet gate. It is garish and loses any vegetation reading. The light brand probe turns the hedge teal with an orange gate, which also no longer reads as planting.
The gate toggle and footprint/grid alignment are not evidenced. All renders show the gate, and nothing shows a no-gate run or tiling against neighbours.
grades.lesson: Make the object's material identity read at thumbnail size from silhouette and surface treatment, not from the label. Organic elements need irregular edges or texture break-up. Small regularly spaced marks on flat faces will be read as windows, so vary or cluster them if they mean something else.

flaws: Hedge geometry doesn't fill its 6x1 footprint. A darker flat ground plane shows through beside the gate and at the far right end in every render. The hedge reads as hollow or unfinished, and at max height the gap becomes an obvious dark slab inside the hedge.

The gate doesn't scale with the height knob. At 1.8 m the posts and pickets stay at the default size, the left post is swallowed by the hedge behind it, and the gate looks like a toy wedged into a wall.
Flower cubes overhang the hedge silhouette at segment edges, most visibly at the right end and top corners, so they look like they are floating rather than growing on the hedge.
A black or dark-green plinth corner sticks out under the left end of the kerb. It is near-black in Formal and dark in both brand probes, and it reads as a z-fighting or leftover base mesh.
The topiary option adds two lumpy stepped blocks on only two segments and removes most of the flowers. It reads as random overhangs, not clipped topiary, and doesn't feel intentional.
The dark brand probe recolours the gate to maroon and the flowers to saturated cyan on lime leaves. It looks garish and off the Oasis Town palette. Brand colour hits the wrong parts.
Segment faces are stacked with near-identical inset panels that look like cabinet doors rather than clipped foliage. The leaf surface has no texture variation, so the hedge reads as green furniture.
grades.lesson: When a knob drives a primary dimension (height, length, depth), derive every attached element from that same value: posts, gates, trims, decorations. Then render the extremes and check that solids still close their footprint with no gaps showing ground through them.

flaws: The two hedge segments do not share an alignment line. The left run sits flush with the front of the base. The right run is pushed back, leaving a large empty white wedge of slab in front of it and to its right. It reads as unfinished geometry and will not tile cleanly with neighbouring 6x1 pieces.
The white base slab is far wider than the hedge on the right half. It dominates the composition as a blank plane instead of reading as a path or kerb.
The right gate post is set back and half-buried in the hedge, while the left post stands proud. The gate leaf floats in front of the gap with no clear hinge relationship to either post.
The face detailing is regular rectangular blocks that read as a stone or brick wall painted green, not as clipped foliage.
The tiny cube clusters on top of a 'clipped' hedge read as stray debris or flowers. They contradict the formal clipped brief.
In the dark brand probe the brand colour is mapped onto the flowers (saturated blue) and the gate wood (brick red). The result is blue flowers and red timber, which looks broken rather than on-brand.
In the light brand probe the flowers turn orange, so the same naturalistic-detail-takes-brand-colour problem appears there too.
The Autumn preset is nearly indistinguishable from the defaults: slightly yellower green and red dots, with no autumnal foliage.
The Formal preset is only a darker green, so the presets add almost no range.
At max height the gate leaf grows to roughly post height and the hinge hardware floats. Hedge segments still keep their offset misalignment.
The topiary blocks on the left overhang the hedge's front face rather than sitting centred on the hedge top.
The 'gate toggle' off state is not demonstrated, so a core knob from the brief is unverified.
grades.lesson: For modular run pieces on a grid, make every segment share the same alignment line and size the base to the occupied footprint. Offset segments or leftover empty slab break both composition and tiling with neighbouring pieces.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A rooftop or ground billboard on legs with a bold panel and lamps. Footprint 4x1. Knobs: panel colour, accent colour, height, lights.

flaws: Dark brand probe breaks the piece. The frame, legs, lamps and braces turn near-white on the pale grey ground, so the structure almost disappears.
In the dark brand probe, the lime panel and cyan house are garish. The catwalk stays mid-grey and no longer belongs to the rest of the palette.

The catwalk sits across the lower third of the panel in every render. It cuts off the base of the hero graphic, hiding the house's foundation and part of the door, and it hides the lowest yellow bar in 'stripes'.
Panel artwork is crammed into the top-left of the panel. The house roof and the top stripe collide with the lamp brackets, leaving a large empty blue field to the right.
Preset 'Sky' is pixel-identical to Defaults, so it offers no distinct variant.
In the Tram and light brand probes, the house outline is white on pale pink or pale yellow and the door is a white sliver. The icon reads washed out, with weak edge definition.
The brief asks for a 'lights' knob, but no render shows lamps lit or any illumination. The lamps sit as inert grey boxes, so the control is unverifiable or ineffective.
At max, the panel shrinks noticeably as the legs grow. This undermines the stated 4x1 footprint and town-kit scale consistency.
grades.lesson: When structural colours are derived from a brand colour, clamp their luminance so they keep clear contrast against the scene background. Every brand input should still leave the silhouette legible.

flaws: Draw-order error at defaults and on every preset: the front-left leg rises over the lower-left of the panel face and cuts across the base of the house graphic. The leg should sit behind or below the panel, not on top of it.
Legs set to 'pole' leaves the catwalk floating in mid-air. It has no brackets, struts or any attachment to the single pole, so this option is broken.
At maximum, the taller legs make the leg-over-panel overlap more obvious, and the house graphic is cramped against the panel's bottom edge.
The left end of the catwalk overhangs past the structure with no support even in the default leg mode, so it reads as unanchored.

The lights knob from the brief is barely legible. The lamps are small grey boxes on the top edge, and the 'light' is a thin yellow strip with no visible glow or wash on the panel face, so lit and unlit states would hardly differ.
Dark brand probe: the cyan house on a lime panel is garish and low-contrast, and the olive door almost disappears. The accent colour is not checked for contrast against the panel colour.
The lamps sit on top of the frame instead of overhanging the face on arms, which weakens the billboard read and the polish.
The house icon is a fixed, real-estate-specific graphic, and the only alternative is generic stripes. That gives limited reuse for a town kit piece.
Cannot verify the 4x1 footprint or scale parity with town-shop.mjs from these renders. Nothing in the renders demonstrates grid alignment.
grades.lesson: Every attached sub-part (walkways, brackets, signage, lamps) must be structurally anchored to members that exist in every variant of every choice knob, and must layer correctly against the faces it sits in front of or behind. Render each choice option and check that nothing floats and nothing draws over a surface it should sit behind before submitting.

flaws: The panel graphic is undersized and pushed into the left third. About 70% of the 'bold panel' is empty flat colour, so it reads as unfinished, not bold.
The left lamp crowds the tram icon. The icon's hanger line runs up into the lamp housing and the lamp's spill shapes sit on top of the icon. It looks like a collision, not a layout.
Footings are inconsistent. Only the front-left leg gets a concrete pedestal. The other legs disappear into the slab with no base, so the structure looks half-built.
With legs set to 'pole', the single post stops with no footing. It sits on an oversized, empty white slab, which reads as a leftover from the leg variant rather than ground designed for a pole.

At max range the asset gets taller, but the panel shrinks and narrows relative to the frame. The lamps drift off their mounts and the catwalk overhangs on the right. Raising height should not reduce the panel.
In the dark brand probe, the navy frame on an olive panel with a pale cyan icon clashes. Brand colours go straight into structure, panel and accent with no harmony check.
The catwalk and railing dominate the front and visually compete with the panel, which is the point of the asset.

The knobs are only partly what the brief asked for. 'design' and 'legs' are useful, but nothing controls footprint or graphic scale, and lights are not clearly exposed as an on/off control in any render.
grades.lesson: When a parametric object has a 'hero' surface (a sign face, screen or label), size and centre its graphic as a proportion of that surface. Reserve explicit clearance zones for attachments like lamps or brackets so graphic and hardware can never overlap at any knob value.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A carousel with a striped cone roof, central pole and blocky horses on poles. Footprint 6x6. Knobs: roof colours, horses 4-8, lights.

flaws: The roof reads as broken geometry in every render. Behind the striped cone sits a flat skirt in a different colour (green at defaults, salmon in the light probe, lavender in the dark probe). It extends past the cone silhouette. The front panels show the stripe colours and the back shows the rim colour, so the back of the roof looks like a mis-sorted or wrong-faced plate rather than a continuous cone.
The central pole is not a pole. It renders as two flat yellow slabs that read as planks or a sign, not the column the brief asks for.
At defaults only three horses are clearly readable, although the knob minimum is 4. One horse is lost behind the centre, or the minimum is not honoured.
At max horses (8) the horses are bunched toward the front, overlap each other and the centre column, and the poles pierce neighbouring horses. Spacing around the ring is uneven and cluttered.
The Fairground preset is pixel-identical to the defaults, so it is a wasted preset.
The Blossom preset washes out. Its pale pink on white makes the roof stripes nearly invisible, and the grey skirt makes the piece look unfinished rather than soft.
In the dark brand probe the horses turn near-black on the brown floor. Their silhouettes muddy, and the black roof wedges merge with the horse colour.
The lights knob has almost no visible effect. The bulbs are a handful of tiny yellow cubes at the roof edge that are indistinguishable at 512px.
The brand colours are applied to the horses' bodies and saddles in ways that drift from the town-shop palette consistency the brief requires.
grades.lesson: For radial or rotationally symmetric 3D pieces, render every face of a ring or cone with the same material logic and per-face depth sorting, then check the back half against the front half at defaults and in each colour probe. A colour or silhouette mismatch between near and far sides almost always signals a sorting or face-selection bug, not a style choice.

flaws: The horses, the element that makes this a carousel, barely read from the kit camera. The low canopy hides most of them, and the few visible ones are tiny white blobs crowded at the front. The asset reads as a striped tent on a platform.

Geometry pokes past the canopy rim at the back-left and back-right in every render. It shows as green at defaults, pink in Tram and purple in the dark probe, and looks like a trim or valance band leaking through the roof edge.
The entrance steps are a flat slab jammed into the platform rim with a dark crevice. They do not sit cleanly on the base and look tacked on.

The 'every range knob at max' render looks almost identical to defaults: only stripe count and horse count change. The lights knob has no visible effect, and the extra horses are still mostly hidden under the roof.
The light cubes stay the same pale yellow in every palette. In the dark probe they float disconnected over a near-black and lime roof, and that roof reads harsh rather than designed.
The poles at the back fade into the canopy shadow. The front poles look like they hold up the roof rather than run through the horses, so the 'horses on poles' motif is not legible.
grades.lesson: Check the asset from the kit's fixed camera and ask whether its defining feature reads first. If a roof, wall or canopy hides the signature element, raise, open up or rescale the occluder until the element is clearly visible in the default render.

flaws: Horses do not read as horses at kit scale. They are white voxel lumps with a coloured saddle and could be sheep or cows. The main subject of a carousel is the least legible part of the asset, while the roof dominates the silhouette.

Dark brand probe breaks the town palette. Saturated cyan is pushed onto the horse poles and centre pole, and electric violet onto the base trim ring. Against the lime roof the piece looks garish and no longer sits beside the other town kit pieces.
Light brand probe keeps a terracotta base rim under a teal roof. The base colour does not follow the brand, so the piece looks half-recoloured.
The 'lights' knob has no visible effect in any render, including max. Only a few tiny dots appear at the roof rim, so a buyer cannot see what the knob does.
At 8 horses the platform becomes crowded. Horses and poles overlap each other in the iso view, with the front horses clustered against the centre column and rim.
Presets are only roof hue swaps (red, green, blue). No preset varies horses, lights or proportions, so the parametric range on show is very thin.
Knob set is minimal for a paid parametric asset. There is no control for roof stripe count, platform trim colour or horse colour, which are what a designer would reach for to fit it into a scene.
grades.lesson: When mapping brand colours onto an asset, apply the primary brand hue to the one or two hero surfaces only. Derive every structural and trim colour as tonal variants of the hero or from the fixed kit palette, never by dropping raw secondary brand hues onto poles, rims and bases. Then check the probe render beside a sibling kit piece to confirm it still belongs to the set.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A small tram station platform 6x3 with a canopy, a bench, a clock and a sign. Knobs: canopy colour, sign colour, lights.

flaws: The brief asks for a bench, but at defaults and in every preset and brand probe there is no readable bench. Only a thin brown strip sits on the back wall. A recognisable bench appears only when every range knob is at maximum.
At maximum, the clock post passes straight through the bench and the clock face overlaps the bench back. This is a clear prop collision.
The 'Tram' preset is pixel-identical to the defaults, so it adds nothing.
The clock reads as a serrated gear or saw blade. Its toothed rim and single tick mark do not say 'clock' at this scale.
The long canopy rests on one front post at the far left. The right end looks unsupported, and the structure feels unresolved.
The sign is tiny and the 'T' glyph is barely legible. As the canopy grows at maximum, the sign shrinks further and gets lost under the eave.
The flat-roof variant reads as stacked loose slabs with a dark band peeking out below, not as a finished canopy.

The knobs do not clearly map to the brief: there is no evident lights toggle in any render. Range knobs scale canopy length rather than offering the controls a designer would expect, such as bench on/off and prop positions.
grades.lesson: Every element named in the brief must be clearly visible at defaults. Give each prop a fixed slot on the footprint that is checked for collisions at both extremes of every knob, so props never appear only at extremes and never pass through each other.

flaws: The 'every range knob at maximum' render is pixel-identical to defaults. The continuous knobs, such as lights, have no visible effect, so a buyer drags sliders and nothing happens.

At defaults the bench, which the brief requires, is almost entirely hidden behind the shelter's back panel. Only a thin brown sliver is visible, so the hero view does not show one of the four specified props.
The hanging lights read as floating yellow cheese-wheel discs below the canopy, not luminaires. There is no glow, no fixture, and no visible cord connecting them to the roof.
The sign's 'text' is three dark blocks beside the T glyph. It reads as placeholder, not a deliberate pictogram, and is too crude for a paid kit piece.
The sign panel is bolted across the roof eave and intersects the canopy edge, so the joinery looks unresolved, especially on the hipped roof.

The dark brand probe produces neon lime on cyan over a grey slab. It is garish, clashes with the warm yellow door panel and tactile strip, and reads as broken palette mapping rather than a dark-brand variant.
In the 'shelter left' layout the planter is tucked behind the shelter and half-occluded. The right two-thirds of the platform is left as empty white slab, which unbalances the composition.
The hipped roof's end face renders as a pale, semi-washed tone in every colourway. It looks like a transparency artefact rather than a shading decision.
grades.lesson: Before shipping, render every knob at its minimum and maximum and diff against defaults. Any knob that produces no visible change must either be wired up or removed. Also confirm every element named in the brief is clearly visible in the default camera view.

flaws: The sign's pixel lettering is malformed. 'TRAM' reads as 'TRAI' or 'TRAł' in every render because the M glyph collapses at this size. The sign is the focal element, so the asset reads as a typo.
At defaults the clock head sits directly on top of the canopy's front post. The two silhouettes merge into a cluttered knot at the front corner instead of reading as two separate objects.
Setting the clock knob to 'right' leaves the planter tree poking out from behind the shelter wall, half-hidden and apparently intersecting the structure. That counts as a broken render.
Setting the clock knob to 'right' also reshuffles the ticket machine and bin to the front-left. This crowds the shelter entrance and makes the layout look arbitrary.
The default bench is only a seat plank with one dark end panel and no back. It looks unfinished next to the full bench shown at max.
The 'lights' knob required by the brief has no visible effect in any render. No lamps, glow or lit sign appear anywhere.
Pushing every range knob to its maximum changes only the bench, so the range knobs are thin. Canopy depth, platform length and sign text are not exposed.
In the light brand probe the sign keeps its default yellow while the canopy follows the brand. The sign colour knob does not seem to respond to the brand theme the way the canopy does.
grades.lesson: Whenever a choice knob relocates one prop, re-solve the placement of every prop against the structure's footprint and each other, then check the render for objects hidden behind or intersecting walls. Never just swap two positions and assume the rest still fits.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A four-to-six storey apartment block with balconies and plants, a lobby door and rooftop water tank. Knobs: wall, balcony colour, floors 3-7, width 4-6 m, water tank toggle, lights.

flaws: Broken geometry at the ground floor in every render. The lower-left corner of the left facade is replaced by a stepped white patch where the base plinth or ground plate shows through the wall, leaving the windows floating on white. It is subtle on the pale defaults but glaring on the black wall in the dark brand probe and still visible at night.

The wall colour knob only recolours the left facade. The balcony facade stays cream in Harbour, the light probe and the dark probe, so a black brand colour gives a black-and-cream building that reads as two different structures.
The dark brand probe looks garish: lime balconies on pure black with a cream right face and a white ground-floor hole. The tinting gives the brand colours no shading or tonal control.

The right facade is cluttered at thumbnail scale. The balcony railings, plants and window bands merge into a busy red or blue stripe with little hierarchy, and the lobby awning is cramped against the lowest balcony.
Presets are near-duplicates. Terracotta differs from the defaults only by a slightly darker balcony red, so it adds almost no range.
At max floors the building gets thinner and taller but the width change is hard to read. The roof stair box and water tank stay the same size and start to look like fussy toy details.

Window lighting is uneven in a way that does not look intentional. The lower floors on the left face are always unlit grey-blue in day renders, which reads as a texture error rather than a designed choice.
grades.lesson: During development, render every kit piece with a very dark and a very saturated wall colour, not only pale defaults. Light palettes hide intersecting ground plates, untinted faces and z-fighting that become obvious the moment a brand colour is applied.

flaws: Dark brand probe breaks the form. A black wall colour flattens both visible faces to the same near-black. Face shading, floor bands and window sills vanish, and the block reads as a flat silhouette instead of an isometric volume.

The wall colour knob only reaches part of the building. The recessed facade behind the balconies stays cream in every variant: Harbour grey, light probe and dark probe. A black building with a cream inner wall looks like a bug, not a choice.
Preset Kyoto renders pixel-identical to defaults, so it is either broken or meaningless.
The water tank is mostly hidden behind the roof slab at default width. Only its cap shows, which undercuts a feature the brief names.
At Night the water tank and roof almost disappear into the navy background. The rooftop silhouette is lost.
The lime balconies on black in the dark probe have no shading or edge definition. They read as flat stickers next to the rest of the shaded geometry.
Nothing in the renders lets me verify the brief's requirement to match town-shop.mjs scale and palette.
grades.lesson: Derive every shaded face and secondary tone from the user's colour with a lightness shift that also works for near-black and near-white inputs (lighten when the base is dark), and make sure every surface belonging to a colour role actually follows that knob. Verify both with extreme brand colours before shipping.

flaws: Dark brand probe: with a near-black wall, the floor bands and panel seams on the street face vanish. The facade becomes a flat black slab with punched windows and loses the storey rhythm that makes it read as an apartment block.
Dark brand probe: the recessed balcony bay keeps its cream/grey interior walls while the outer faces turn black. The building reads as two unrelated materials, not one recoloured block.
Plants, a named feature in the brief, are tiny green specks at every setting. At defaults they are barely visible, and against the green/lime balcony probes and at night they disappear entirely.
Max floors (7): the lobby awning crowds up under the lowest balcony, so the entrance stack looks cramped and nearly colliding rather than designed.
The white corner strip between the two faces reads as a gap or rendering seam rather than a deliberate pilaster, especially on the default and Tram renders.
The entrance step slab pokes out past the building footprint as a bright white tile, which may break flush placement on the 6 m town grid.
The width knob (4-6 m) shows little visible change in the max render, so its usefulness at the extremes cannot be confirmed.
grades.lesson: Derive trim, seam and shadow-line colours relative to the base colour's luminance (lighten on dark, darken on light) and recolour every surface that shares the wall role, so structural detail survives any brand colour, not just the default palette.

brief: Oasis Town 3D block kit piece on the 6 m grid, matching town-shop.mjs scale and palette. A round plaza fountain on a 4x4 footprint: stepped stone basin, central column, water as pale blue cylinders. Knobs: stone colour, water colour, tiers 1-3, size.

warnings: knobs with very subtle effect: lights
colour knobs without a brand role: stone, water
